text.title: Freelancer Weekly Report Template Core Rules
text.summary: Seven rules for the four-block weekly report: shipped rows need a resolvable artefact, client-owned work belongs in asks rather than next, risks carry a mitigation and a decision date, asks name one human, progress is counted not estimated, and the cadence is held on the bad weeks too.

rule.statement: Every shipped entry carries a link the client can open: a merged PR URL, a commit SHA, a ticket id, or a deployed URL. A row whose evidence is prose ("worked on the checkout flow") is deleted from the report rather than reworded.

rationale.source: Deliverable-acceptance evidence practice in contract administration

rule.rationale: The shipped list is the document a client re-reads when an invoice is questioned, often months later and often by someone who was not in the thread. An unlinked row cannot be verified by that person, so it is treated as a claim; a merged-PR link moves the discussion from whether the work happened to whether it was the agreed work.

rule.statement: Every next entry names an owner and a calendar date. Any item whose owner is on the client side MUST appear in asks instead, with the same date. A next list containing a client-owned item is rejected.

rationale.source: Schedule management practice — external dependencies tracked with a named owner

rule.rationale: An item awaiting client input that sits in "next" reads to the client as your work in progress, so nobody on their side acts on it. It ages quietly until the deadline, and the slip is then attributed to the freelancer because the report itself said the freelancer owned it.

rule.statement: Each risk entry holds {risk, mitigation, owner} plus the date by which the decision must be taken. A risk with no mitigation is not a risk entry — it moves to asks as a decision request.

rationale.source: Risk register practice (PMBOK — each risk carries a response and a risk owner)

rule.rationale: A risk stated without a response is read as commentary: there is no action attached to it, so it is acknowledged and nothing changes. Its only effect arrives after it fires, when it is quoted back as proof that everyone knew.

rule.statement: Each ask names a single human recipient (not "the team", "stakeholders", "product"), the exact artefact or decision needed, and a needed-by date. Asks addressed to a group or to a role are rejected.

rationale.source: Diffusion of responsibility / bystander effect (Darley & Latané, 1968)

rule.rationale: An ask addressed to several people is answered by none of them — each reads it as somebody else's item and the responsibility is split until it disappears. Naming one recipient removes the ambiguity about who is expected to reply, which is the only variable the report can control.

rule.statement: Progress is reported as completed over total countable units ("8 of 11 endpoints migrated", "3 of 5 screens accepted"). Percent-complete figures for work in flight ("about 80% done") are forbidden anywhere in the report.

rationale.source: Ninety-ninety rule (Tom Cargill, Bell Labs; cited in Bentley, CACM 1985)

rule.rationale: Percent-complete on unfinished work is an unfalsifiable self-assessment, and the residual fraction routinely consumes as much time as everything before it. The client plans hiring, launches and payments against that number believing it is a measurement, so the correction arrives as a broken promise rather than as new information.

rule.statement: cadence_anchor fixes a day, time and timezone, and the report ships in that slot every week of the engagement — including weeks where shipped is empty, which are sent with the reason stated. A skipped week is a rule violation, not a judgement call.
rule.rationale: The report is only informative if its absence means nothing, and it stops meaning nothing the first time a bad week is skipped. From then on the client reads silence as trouble and starts chasing — which is the exact overhead the fixed cadence was bought to remove.

rule.statement: Skip when the engagement is shorter than two weeks (a single closeout report covers it) or when the client has explicitly opted out of a weekly cadence in favour of milestone reports. Emit a structured skip naming which condition held.
rule.rationale: The template's value comes from repetition — week two is where the client stops chasing. On a one-week engagement the report costs the same and buys nothing, and imposing a cadence the client declined turns a trust instrument into noise they filter.
